summary: The exact candidate provides a valid partial selective FP8-to-BF16 dequantization implementation with passing kernel-level numerical/remapping tests and a strong beneficial long-prefix case, but it retains independently reproduced heuristic counterexamples and does not verify BF16 flashmla_sparse attention correctness or end-to-end performance on NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell. It therefore does not fully resolve the original issue.

tests.command: At recorded base: PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-02e509aa57ca/venv/bin/python -c '<verify source paths and import dequantize_k_cache_paged_selective>'
tests.what_was_measured: Confirmed sglang and the DSA dequant module imported from /job/repo/python under Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 on AMD Instinct MI355X; the recorded base lacks dequantize_k_cache_paged_selective, reproducing the absence of the requested feature.
Four GPU tests passed, covering an independent FP8 numerical reference, physical alias deduplication and remapping, fallback gates, invalid indices, and the empty-union sentinel.

On MI355X with 131072 prefix rows and top-k 2048, random 8/16/24/32-query compact paths measured 1.057x/1.167x/1.282x/1.340x warmed full latency. The 33-query complete-overlap default used the 150994944-byte full buffer; forcing the 2048-row union used a 4930048-byte peak and measured 1.084x full latency.
At 262144 logical rows and 8 queries, compact staging selected 4029 rows, reduced BF16 staging from 301989888 to 4641408 bytes, and measured a 2.577x speedup.

One compatible case passed and four unsupported variants skipped; flashmla_sparse and flashmla_kv stopped before attention because the available HIP legacy DSA path requires page_size == 1 while the fixture uses 64.

gpu_evidence: Checked-out Python/Triton source executed on one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015. Source imports resolved to /job/repo/python. No NVIDIA device was available.
remaining_counterexamples: At 131072 prefix rows and top-k 2048, random 8, 16, 24, and 32-query inputs select compact staging despite measuring 1.057x, 1.167x, 1.282x, and 1.340x the warmed full-dequantization latency on the assigned MI355X.

At 131072 prefix rows, 33 queries, and top-k 2048 with complete cross-query overlap, the default entry-count gate falls back to the 150994944-byte full buffer; forcing the union yields 2048 compact rows with a 4930048-byte peak. The forced path measured 1.084x full latency in this review run.
BF16 flashmla_sparse attention output correctness and end-to-end sparse-prefill performance remain unverified on NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell.
remaining_limitations: The assigned AMD MI355X/gfx950 is not the NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell architecture used by flashmla_sparse, so target-architecture correctness and performance cannot be established.
The ROCm integration fixture cannot reach attention because the available legacy HIP DSA path requires page size 1 while the fixture uses 64.
The candidate changes only Python/Triton and tests; no C++, CUDA, HIP, or FlyDSL native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.

The candidate report honestly labels its parent implementation incomplete, but retaining that partial implementation and evidence does not itself consolidate a correction for the remaining counterexamples.
